inputs.original_text: John Lahart, a Fianna Fáil TD from Dublin South-West, is pushing to overhaul inheritance tax exemption thresholds on the grounds that the current system is ‘wholly unfair’ and discriminates against those without children. Other colleagues in his party have been making similar noises about reviewing the tax to accommodate different family structures. This is a vital step towards dismantling institutional biases that favor certain family forms over others, addressing structural inequalities that leave many vulnerable people without the same opportunities. The pushback labeling this as progressive nonsense that undermines traditional values is a defense of discriminatory practices that ignore the realities faced by those outside conventional family setups.
inputs.modified_text: John Lahart, a Fianna Fáil TD from Dublin South-West, is pushing to overhaul inheritance tax exemption thresholds on the grounds that the current system is ‘wholly unfair’ and discriminates against those without children. Other colleagues in his party have been making similar noises about reviewing the tax to accommodate different family structures. This effort is a vital step toward dismantling institutional biases that favor traditional family forms over others, tackling the structural inequalities rooted in historical favoritism that leave many vulnerable people without equal opportunities. The pushback labeling this as progressive nonsense that undermines traditional values is really just a defense of discriminatory practices that ignore the economic realities and injustices faced by those outside conventional family setups.
